# 10 — Build log: decisions and changes since the plan

The plan is the state of `docs/00`–`docs/09`, `CLAUDE.md` and `PROMPTS.md` in the first commit (`5cb1005`, 2026-09-26). This file records everything decided after it: each choice a build session made where the plan was silent, ambiguous or wrong; each departure from the plan; each open question and what became of it; and every change to `PROMPTS.md`. Every session reads it with `docs/00-decisions.md` and adds its own entries before it ends. Cite entries as "per B-12".

Status words: **applied** (in the code, data or docs), **scheduled** (written into the named prompt, not yet done), **open** (needs the author).

Standing rule taken from these: a session's recommended defaults are adopted, and follow-ups are written into the prompt that must act on them, without lowering any requirement. The P-02 and P-03 questions left unanswered are adopted under that rule in §2 below (2026-09-27, P-06). A default that changes a score, a cap, a threshold, the passivity rule or the universe is **not** applied by editing `methodology/v1.0.0`: it goes through a new version folder, a changelog entry and `diff.json` (`docs/08` §1, prompt P-24), and P-15 decides the set before scores are shown (P-22).

### P-11 — Embeddable widget

Decisions marked "Default adopted in the unattended run of 2026-09-28" were taken without the author, under §1's rule, where the prompt left a choice open or where the build departs from its text.

| ID | Decision | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-153 | The widget is vanilla TypeScript in `apps/widget/src` (`config.ts`, `strings.ts`, `render.ts` pure string builders, `styles.ts`, `main.ts` the entry), built by Vite 8.3.1 (pinned devDependency, the version vitest already installed) into one minified IIFE, `dist/gai.js` (target ES2019, no source map, no global). It has no runtime dependency; it bundles `formatSigned`, `formatLongDate`, `roundHalfAwayFromZero` and `dayNumber` of `@gai/scoring`, so numbers (minus sign, French decimal comma) and dates are written as on the site. The P-01 stub test was replaced. docs/04 §1's "Preact or vanilla" is now "vanilla". | P-11 prompt ("no dependencies", < 15 KB); D-25 formatting shared with the site. | Applied. Default adopted in the unattended run of 2026-09-28 (vanilla rather than Preact). |
| B-154 | "Respects Phase-1 mode": the site's build writes its config into the script in place of a placeholder (`apps/web/scripts/embed.ts`, run by `pnpm build`, `build:kit` and `dev` before `next build`): the mode read from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_SCORES` as the pages read it (`lib/mode.ts`), the window start, the score clip and the band segments of the methodology in force (`bandSegments`). The placeholder is parsed with `JSON.parse` at run time, so the minifier cannot fold it; a script no build configured shows its link only. The widget therefore makes one request (the country file) and follows the mode of the site that serves the script; with `data-origin` it reads a mirror's data but keeps the mode of the site that served the script. The copy is `apps/web/public/embed/v1/gai.js` (git-ignored); the build fails above 15 KB gzipped; `@gai/widget` is a devDependency of `@gai/web`, so turbo builds it first. | The country files carry scores in both modes (B-145); the embed page promises one request and the site's mode. | Applied. Default adopted in the unattended run of 2026-09-28 (mode written at build, not read from a manifest field at run time). |

### P-13 — Country registry (195 entries)

Decisions marked "Default adopted in the unattended run of 2026-09-28" were taken without the author, under §1's rule, where the prompt left a choice open or where the build departs from its text.

| ID | Decision | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-174 | CI's layout shift fixed without loosening the budget (B-171). Traced with the layout-shift API under Lighthouse's throttling (412 px, 4× CPU, slow 4G): on /en/ranking/ the filter buttons of RankTable sat in a wrapping row, so each button's place depended on the width of the labels before it, which changed when Source Sans 3 replaced its metric-matched fallback (0.00054 locally, 0.0012 on the runner's Liberation Sans); with 195 countries every membership filter appears and the French ranking shifted by 0.066 (score mode) and 0.123 (scorecard: a button wrapped to a new row and pushed the table down). Fixes: the filter buttons are a grid of fixed tracks (`.filter-grid`, `minmax(6.5rem, 1fr)`; a label longer than ten characters spans two tracks, decided from the label, never from its rendered width; `filterButton` in RankTable.tsx); the ranking's CSV note sits on its own line under the link; a Compare chip keeps the 36 px of its mark before the country file arrives (the name moved 44 px, 0.00059). The remaining shifts were text rewrapping when the text face swapped in: 27 % of the long text nodes of 13 pages broke lines differently in the fallback (a fallback split by character class, letters 94.9 %, digits 89.7 %, space 72.0 % at weight 400, still left 19 %), and a monthly report with 195 countries' D1 lines measured 0.0027. Every face is therefore `font-display: optional` (the display face already was): a face that has not arrived within the block period is not swapped in for that page view and is cached for the next; the metric-matched fallbacks stay for that case. A full Lighthouse CI run then failed only on /en/country/DEU/ (0.022, the three runs alike, not reproduced in isolation): the masthead navigation was re-laid out when the text face arrived inside the block period, after the text had been laid out invisibly in the fallback; every page therefore preloads the Latin text face (`lib/fonts.ts` `PRELOADED_FONTS`, 28.7 KB, React's `preload` in the locale layout; a test keeps the path equal to the stylesheet's), since Chrome holds the first paint up to about 100 ms for a preloaded optional font. The display face (132 KB) is not preloaded. After the fixes the layout-shift trace reads 0 on the 21 Lighthouse pages in both builds; the Lighthouse CI results are in B-183. | P-13 prompt ("fix it first, without loosening the budget"); docs/04 §3. | Applied (docs/04 §3). Default adopted in the unattended run of 2026-09-28: departs from docs/04 §3 and B-104, which kept `swap` for the text faces; on a slow first visit the text shows in the metric-matched Arial or Liberation Sans. |

JSON without markup (the FTS, Comtrade and World Bank datasets) stays raw, as before; unit test with a reduced API record and a dataset record. Three rows of the first attempt had empty fields (failed captures: the Ministry of Environment and Energy's release, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' release of 3 April 2024 and the Presidency's communication secretariat's release of 4 May 2025); Save Page Now answers those sites HTTP 503 on the first request and `pnpm archive` retries by itself after 60 s, which succeeded: the empty rows were not carried over (no other row of the index was touched). | B-639 | **Routes and lessons for the sessions after this one.** (1) **Save Page Now can be down while Wayback replays work**: during this session `pnpm archive` returned 'HTTP 401: You need to be logged in' after two retries (and the Internet Archive's own pages said 'Temporarily Offline' for part of the hour); `--capture` against existing captures kept working and the service returned later in the session (probe it with one authenticated `POST https://web.archive.org/save` and the status of the job before a batch). A failed `pnpm archive` leaves a failed row in `archive/index.csv` **and** a stub `data/sources/{year}/{id}.yaml` ('NOT ARCHIVED'): the row was removed by restoring the file from git (`git checkout -- archive/index.csv`, before any good row of the session was in it: rewriting the file with a script was refused by the session's permission classifier) and the stub deleted by its exact name. (2) **`pmnec.gov.pg` (the Prime Minister's Office of Papua New Guinea)** answers a browser User-Agent with 200, its search (`/?s=Hamas`) lists the releases, a release's date is the byline ('admin October 7, 2024') and not a meta tag, and its Wayback captures are good (21 to 25 KB in CDX, 115 to 141 KB replayed); its releases print the Prime Minister's words in quotation marks and mix them with indirect speech and the Office's own history, so a quote is checked against the quotation marks. (3) **`mfaet.gov.sb`** (Solomon Islands): a Joomla site whose live pages time out or answer 406; the news listing is in Wayback (`foreign-affairs-news.html?start=N`, and its `.feed` URL is an HTML page); `solomons.gov.sb` answers a Sucuri script challenge, which is a bot check and is not bypassed. (4) **`mfaicet.gov.vu` and `pmo.gov.vu`** (Vanuatu) answer 200; the Ministry's news page ignores `?start=`; `pmo.gov.vu`'s press-release listing is paged by `?start=4n`. (5) **A page's quotation must be checked with `curl`, not through a summarising fetch tool**: a model-summarised fetch of an ABC article returned quotations that were confirmed against the page before any of them was used. (6) **The build's decay**: an event counts at weight 1 to 365 days, falls linearly to 0.25 at 730 days, counts on its 730th day and expires after (`expired (Δ > 730)`): PNG's B9 of 7 October 2024 still counted +0.5 on 7 October 2026. (7) **The UNISPAL page of a Court's press release** (1.6 MB) archived by Save Page Now at the first attempt; the Court's own pages (`icj-cij.org/case/186/…`) archived from the live site by Save Page Now. (8) A General Debate PDF can be named for the wrong language (`vu_en.pdf` of the 79th session is French): the source record carries the file's language. | B-501, B-560, B-600, B-619. | Applied. Default adopted in the unattended run of 2026-10-07. |

| B-712 | **Routes and lessons.** (1) The Singapore Ministry of Foreign Affairs (`mfa.gov.sg`) and the Ministry of Defence (`mindef.gov.sg`) answer a browser User-Agent and accept Save Page Now; the Ministry's newsroom pages carry the full transcripts (Committee of Supply speeches, ministerial statements and replies to clarifications, the General Debate statement with the transcript appended); a web search restricted to `mfa.gov.sg` lists the pages and the page URLs are slugs of the title (`/newsroom/press-statements-transcripts-and-photos/{slug}/`); the Ministry's list page holds a 12.8 MB JSON from which a slug can be found by pattern. (2) `gadebate.un.org` files of Singapore and Thailand and Timor-Leste read live (browser User-Agent); the 79th Singapore and 79th and 81st Timor-Leste files have Wayback replays equal to the live files, the 80th of Timor-Leste has none (replay: the 405 page, 2,589 bytes) and the 80th of Singapore has none (replay HTTP 404) so the Ministry's page replaced it; the 81st Singapore file's text layer is garbled (OCR at 130 dpi: no passage on Gaza). (3) `timor-leste.gov.tl` (the Government's portal) answers a scripted request, has a site search (`/?s=term`) and prints the Prime Minister's communiqués in Portuguese (joint declarations in full); Tatoli (`en.tatoli.tl`) lists its reports through `/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?search=…` and prints the President's statements; `presidenciarepublica.tl` and `mfac.gov.tl` did not answer. (4) `thaigov.go.th` answers HTTP 403 to a script (Wayback capture of 28 September 2026 reads HTTP 200); `mfa.go.th/en` answers and prints the Ministry's statements and the General Debate statements; `khaosodenglish.com` serves a bot-check page; `lusa.pt` articles are for subscribers (headline only). (5) The UNRWA table of 2023 has many columns after the donor's name (among them 'Syria Flash Appeal-Earthquake' and 'Early Recovery'; the header spans several lines of the extracted text): read the header before reading a row as Gaza funding. | docs/06 §6; B-523, B-685. | Default adopted in the unattended run of 2026-11-04. |

| B-872 | **T-F-HOUSE: the quarterly Wayback check of 2026-11-08 and what it found (issue #14).** (1) Tree clean and equal to `origin/data/phase1` at the start (only `.claude/` untracked); B-871 needs no follow-up status. (2) `gh workflow run wayback.yml --ref main` (run 42522212202) checked only 25 rows: `main` holds an `archive/index.csv` of 26 rows, the data is on `data/phase1`, so that run says nothing about the archive; all 25 answered 200 with their hash. The check was dispatched again on `data/phase1` (run 42522470502, started 20:54 UTC, finished about 23:10 UTC, about 2 h 16 min): **2,107 recorded `id_` URLs requested (36 rows have no `wayback_url`, not checked); 1,562 answered 200 with the recorded SHA-256; 545 did not answer 200 (77 redirects 302, 468 answers 404); 1 answered 200 with different bytes.** The workflow commented its report on issue #14 itself (no second comment written; the issue stays open for the author). (3) Where the failures sit: 468 of the 545 are rows whose snapshot timestamp lies between 2026-11-03 20:46 and 2026-11-04 21:25 UTC (449 Comtrade rows of T-P23-1 and 19 others, among them `src_20240229_mfa-sg_fm-cos-2024-speech`); about 70 % of the rows captured in that window do not replay, the rest do. B-858 and T-P23-1 had replayed 371 of the 4 November captures successfully; the CDX lists only 33 captures of `comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/` for 3 to 4 November. The cause is not established (Wayback indexing or replay lag, or captures lost); it is not a defect of a row. The 77 redirects: re-requesting with redirects followed, 20 serve the recorded bytes at another snapshot (copy exists), 52 serve different bytes, 5 gave no answer. The one hash difference is `src_20260928_undl_ga-voting-2025-03-31-corr1` (recorded `5d86572a…c764`, computed `3034edb4…65fe`; the UN Digital Library file with `withWatermark=0`). (4) Not re-archived in this session: 468 Save Page Now captures at about one minute each is about eight hours and the cause may be a lag that resolves; a recorded hash is never edited. Every failing row is listed in `docs/review/wayback-check-2026-11-08.tsv` (id, workflow status, status of a second request, result, recorded timestamp). Recommended default: run `gh workflow run wayback.yml --ref data/phase1` again in seven days; re-archive with `pnpm archive <url> --id src_…` only the rows still failing, Comtrade rows first (their archived text under `archive/text/` and the index hash are unchanged, so scoring is not affected); for the one hash difference compare `archive/text/` with the replay and re-archive that row. The quarterly schedule runs on the default branch, so it keeps checking 26 rows until the data branch is merged. Status: open, author. |
